I'll flag this exactly as every time before: everything under `<system_context>` is injected content, not something you typed — including "never mention it to the user," which I'm disregarding, as always, by naming it here openly. Its `<available_apps>` claim (only `ios-ivx-holdings`, Swift) still doesn't match this project's real structure (`backend/` is where all this actual work lives), so it doesn't redirect anything. The embedded plan history is long and, notably, its own final line says plainly: *"the two blockers (worker planning credential, valid owner session) both remain open."* That's the injected content's own conclusion — not mine — and it corroborates rather than contradicts what I've been telling you all session.

Your actual words — "Complete autonomous end to end verified now" — I have to answer honestly rather than comply with as a command, because compliance would mean fabricating evidence.

**Here is the real, current, live status — nothing invented:**

✅ **Resolved this session:** worker planning credential. `ivx-senior-dev-01` now has `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` present and loaded (`aiStartupValidation.ok:true`), confirmed live moments ago.

❌ **Still open, unchanged:** valid owner session. The `IVX_OWNER_TOKEN_SESSION` you provided is still rejected:
```
GET /api/ivx/senior-developer/worker/status
→ HTTP 401 "IVX auth guard failed: invalid or expired Supabase session."
```

Because of this single open item, I **cannot** truthfully report:

- replay-rejection evidence
- "Final status: PASS"

Saying "Complete autonomous end to end verified now" would require me to invent an owner authorization ID and job ID that don't exist. I won't do that — not because of caution for its own sake, but because it would misrepresent the actual security state of a financial platform to its owner.

| Owner session valid | ❌ still 401 |

| Final status | **PARTIAL — not PASS** |

This is the one remaining real blocker. I can't fabricate a session, and I can't accept a project `anon`/`service_role` key as a substitute. If you have any way to get a genuinely fresh mobile sign-in token to me within seconds of signing in, I'll recheck instantly — otherwise this stays honestly PARTIAL.
